title: Python: a lazy class-body read (alias value, or an alias type parameter's bound, constraint or default) of a name the class body binds anywhere never resolves through an enclosing scope, a star import or a builtin; it refuses (DEC-303 (a76), folds N1a and N1b)
description: HOLD, wrong claims on dev. WIDENED under DEC-303 (a76) (relayed by the leader 2026-11-27; supersedes this task's first scope). One rule: a LAZY class-body read, meaning an alias value or an alias type parameter's bound, constraint or default, of a name the class body binds ANYWHERE never resolves through an enclosing scope, a star import or a builtin. It REFUSES. Removal-only per (a73) item 2: it does NOT resolve to the class binding (m.len, m.f) because that would create edges. A lazy read runs after the class body, so it sees the class's FINAL binding; dev claims otherwise on these measured inputs (origin/dev 4e186bfb, identical on the GCLI-144 head; CPython 3.15.2 for the runtime answers). (1) the alias BOUND: class C with def run; x = C() at module level or in def outer(); class Outer: type A[T: x.run()] = int; from m import X as x: dev edges [C, C.run] (calls 2), runtime the bound reads m.X; the same for the constraint tuple type A[T: (x.run(), int)] = int. (2) N1a: m.py def len(o): pass; app.py class Outer: type A = len([]); from m import len: dev bins external 1, no edge (claims the BUILTIN len), runtime Outer.A.__value__ is m.len. (3) N1b: s.py def f(): pass; m.py def f(): pass; app.py from s import *; class Outer: type A = f(); from m import f: dev gives the edge app.py:3:14 to s.py:f, runtime m.f. Twins on dev: def f[T: x.run()](self) and class K[T: x.run()] in a class body record only x = C() (bounds of a def or class are not walked: GCLI-145, ordinary). Module-level type A[T: x.run()] = int with a single module x = C() gives C.run, correct there. MECHANISM (GCLI-144's marker, Scope.lazyAlias, already exists): walk an alias's type parameter bound, constraint and default in its lazy scope; and in lookupBindings a lazy read where Rule 38 dropped the class binding refuses even when nothing is bound further out, so the lookup must not return null (unbound, builtin, star) for it: that is the 'lazyDiffers && bindings.length > 0' condition pinned by GCLI-147, whose N1a and N1b fixtures this task turns from 'unchanged from dev' into REFUSED. PROOF: fixtures for the bound and constraint forms plus N1a and N1b, each red on dev and green after; a mutant per path, run red; the subset check, every head edge a dev edge and no new builtin or star claim, over the five pins, the fixtures and the 450-source corpus (add bound, constraint, default and builtin or star sources). Two review rounds (DEC-161). ORDER: after #225 and GCLI-147, before GCLI-140 (the (a25) attribute-write rule); the (a36) item 8 pre-registration, GCLI-143, waits. Stays hold until the leader starts it. Not started.
